text:
maya: starting a thread for the "brokered prepack" experiment. idea: introduce a lightweight broker in the router layer that negotiates prepack admits with runtime rather than blind coalescing. goal = reduce enqueue jitter for tiny chats but keep headroom signals and fairness intact.
aj: Nice name. how does the broker differ from router-first packing we tried earlier?
maya: Router still coalesces candidates into a prepack envelope, but before sending it to runtime the broker opens a tiny handshake: it asks runtime for a pack admit token (fast RPC) that reflects current headroom. runtime replies OK/DEFER or a suggested split size. if DEFER, router partial-unpacks and sends per-item fastpaths.
carmen: That sounds promising for not hiding headroom. Does it add latency for the fast path? we need <1ms overhead ideally.
maya: Bench: broker rpc adds ~0.6ms median on-hop in our env (edge->controlplane hop), but it avoids wasted large envelope requeues which cost much more. We'll canary to measure.
li: Fairness question: will broker tokens be fungible across tenants? could still allow a noisy tenant to claim large admits.
maya: Broker issues per-tenant lease tokens. basic policy: tokens proportional to tenant soft-credit; broker refuses cross-tenant aggregation past a fraction. config example below.
wayne: paste the config pls.
maya: ```yaml
broker_prepack:
  enabled: true
  pack_window_ms: 5
  max_pack_items: 14
  broker_rpc_timeout_ms: 5
  per_tenant_lease_fraction: 0.6  # fraction of pack items allowed to belong to single tenant
  min_tokens_to_pack: 4
  small_bypass_tokens: 12
  headroom_refresh_ms: 200
  async_kv_prefetch: true
  prefix_hint_len: 28
```
aj: Observability: new metrics we need: `broker.admits`, `broker.defers`, `broker.split_suggestions`, and trace tag `X-Broker-Trace`. correlate with `runtime.headroom_samples` and `runtime.kv_miss_rate`.
carmen: Rollout plan idea: region-scoped canary 5% -> 20%. Canary guardrails: p99 latency, runtime.kv_miss_rate, and per-tenant skew. auto-degrade if p99 up >7% or kv_miss delta >2.5%.
li: Important handshake: runtime should return suggested pack_size when under pressure instead of just DEFER. router can then send smaller envelopes. avoids full unpack.
maya: runtime RPC response proto sketch:```proto
message PackAdmitResp {
  enum Status { OK = 0; DEFER = 1; SUGGEST_SPLIT = 2; }
  Status status = 1;
  int32 allowed_pack_items = 2; // used when SUGGEST_SPLIT
  bool warm_kv = 3; // advise prefetch
}
```
wayne: Nice. what about long-seq hazard? if a long doc sneaks into a pack we could pay huge token-cost.
maya: Broker inspects length bins and rejects mixes with >X token variance. default rule: only coalesce if max_tokens_in_group / median_tokens_in_group < 3. also prefer same model variant.
aj: Also ensure the broker honors runtime eviction hints. if runtime signals frequent eviction events, broker should reduce pack window to 0 for that shard.
maya: agreed, `eviction_rate` will factor into broker scoring.
carmen: Debugging: packed envelopes make logs noisy. include `unpacked_sample_id` with 1/1000 sampling and attach original request ids to traces. add an unpack reconstruction job for postmortem.
li: For dedicated clusters we may want to expose broker as opt-in per-tenant. some customers will prefer no router coalescing.
maya: Will add rollout flagging.
devops-bot: deploy: canary scheduled infra-canary-21 in 15m. watching: broker.admits, broker.defers, runtime.kv_miss_rate, p99_latency, eviction_rate. auto-rollback rules enabled.
wayne: test harness: mixed synthetic workload: 70% tiny chats (<=18 tokens), 20% medium (50-150 tokens), 10% long (>=400 tokens). include a hot tenant at 45% traffic and a misbehaving tenant that spikes.
maya: test plan posted to PR + dashboards. action items: Maya = push broker PR + dashboards + unpack sampling; Aj = runtime rpc impl + suggested-split logic; Carmen = alerts and canary runbook; Li = per-tenant opt-in flag; Wayne = eval harness + mixed traffic generator.
aj: one more: measure token-cost variance and per-request cost percentile (p50/p95/p99 tokens/req). packing helps latency but can regress cost for some tails — we must quantify.
maya: will add token-cost dashboards and a regression alert (10% delta at p95 tokens/req).
wayne: If canary is clean we can consider folding broker logic into dedicated router for next quarter. but keep runtime API stable.
maya: thanks all. posting PR link shortly. :rocket:
